questions.q: Describe the major physiographic divisions of India.
answer: On the basis of relief and structure, India is divided into six major physiographic units.

answer.text: In the north lie the young fold Himalayas, arranged in three parallel ranges, the lofty Greater Himalayas, the Lesser Himalayas with hill stations, and the outer Shiwaliks. South of them stretches the fertile Northern Plain, built by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.
The Peninsular Plateau, one of the oldest landmasses, is bordered by the Western and Eastern Ghats and includes the Deccan. To its north-west lies the sandy Indian, or Thar, Desert.
Along the seas are the Western and Eastern Coastal Plains, and finally the island groups, the volcanic Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal and the coral Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea.

answer: Together these divisions give India its varied physical framework.

questions.q: Why are the Northern Plains of India of great economic importance?

answer.text: were built by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers, and they are among the most valuable regions of India.

list: The deep, fertile alluvial soil supports intensive agriculture and feeds much of the country
Perennial rivers provide water for irrigation and transport all year

answer.lead: The plains support dense human activity.

list: The level land makes farming, road- and rail-building and settlement easy
So the plains hold a dense population, many great cities, and much of India's industry and trade

questions.q: What is the significance of the Peninsular Plateau in India's geography?

answer.text: is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses on Earth, and it is very important to India.

list: It is rich in minerals like iron ore, coal, manganese and bauxite, forming the base of India's mining and heavy industry
Its black soil is well suited to growing cotton
Its rivers descend from the edges as waterfalls, offering sites for hydroelectric power
Its forests provide timber and shelter wildlife, and its highlands and hills influence climate and rainfall
